summary: Modern databases have evolved to embed AI and ML capabilities natively, eliminating the need to move data to external systems for inference, embedding generation, and vector search. By 2026, vector database adoption has grown 377% year over year, with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search capabilities, driving platforms like Snowflake, BigQuery, and PostgreSQL to integrate LLM functions, embedding pipelines, and similarity search directly into their query engines. The competitive landscape now spans purpose-built vector databases and general-purpose platforms with AI extensions, giving enterprises flexibility to choose based on scale, governance, and infrastructure preferences.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides a suite of serverless LLM functions including COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, SENTIMENT, TRANSLATE, and EMBED_TEXT, all running inside the Snowflake security perimeter without data leaving the platform. Snowflake Postgres now runs natively in the AI Data Cloud with pgvector support, enabling vector similarity search alongside Cortex AI functions for text-to-SQL generation and embedding creation. Cortex Analyst and Cortex Search extend capabilities to natural language querying over structured data and hybrid search over unstructured content.
databases.llm_integration: Native LLM functions via Cortex AI support models including Mistral, LLaMA, and Snowflake Arctic. Cortex Search provides hybrid vector and keyword search. Integration with Snowflake Postgres and pgvector enables embedding-based retrieval pipelines fully within the platform.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits based on token consumption and model size. Larger models consume more credits per call. Snowflake Postgres and vector search capabilities are included in the AI Data Cloud pricing tiers, with general availability announced in early 2026.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data teams to create and execute ML models using standard SQL syntax directly within BigQuery, supporting logistic regression, k-means clustering, matrix factorization, time series forecasting, and deep neural networks. BigQuery's Vertex AI integration enables remote model inference, embedding generation via the ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING function, and vector search through the VECTOR_SEARCH function using approximate nearest neighbor lookup on embedding columns stored natively in BigQuery tables. BigQuery also supports importing and calling Vertex AI foundation models including Gemini directly from SQL.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Google's Gemini model family allows SQL-based calls to foundation models for text generation, classification, and embedding. ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions bring LLM inference into standard BigQuery queries without data movement.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and prediction costs are based on bytes processed or slot usage depending on pricing model. Vector search and embedding generation via Vertex AI integrations incur additional Vertex AI API costs billed per character or per 1,000 characters depending on the model. On-demand and flat-rate slot reservations both apply.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds a native vector data type and supports exact and approximate nearest neighbor search using IVFFlat and HNSW indexing algorithms, making it the lowest-friction path to vector search for teams already running Postgres. pgai is a complementary extension developed by Timescale that brings AI model calling, embedding generation, and LLM inference directly into PostgreSQL via SQL functions, allowing embeddings to be created and kept in sync automatically as data changes. Together they enable full RAG pipelines inside a standard Postgres instance without additional infrastructure, handling production workloads of up to 50 million vectors effectively.
databases.llm_integration: pgai supports integration with OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic Claude, and Cohere APIs directly from SQL. Snowflake Cortex AI functions also integrate with Snowflake-managed Postgres instances running pgvector. pgvectorscale extends HNSW performance for high-throughput embedding workloads.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to use on self-hosted Postgres. Managed offerings such as Supabase, Neon, AWS RDS, and Snowflake Postgres include pgvector with standard instance pricing. LLM API calls made through pgai are billed directly by the respective AI provider at their standard rates.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.description: Aurora ML integrates Amazon Aurora databases with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock, enabling SQL-based invocation of ML models and foundation LLMs for inference directly from database queries, including use cases like fraud detection, sentiment analysis, and content generation. Redshift ML uses Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to automatically train, tune, and deploy ML models from Redshift data using CREATE MODEL SQL statements, supporting binary classification, regression, and multi-class classification. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL also supports the pgvector extension for vector similarity search, enabling RAG workflows and semantic search within the managed Aurora environment.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora ML integrates with Amazon Bedrock to invoke foundation models including Claude, Titan, and Llama 2 directly from SQL. Redshift ML connects to SageMaker for model training and inference endpoints. Both services keep data within the AWS security boundary during inference.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference costs are based on SageMaker endpoint usage or Bedrock token consumption depending on the model invoked. Redshift ML charges for SageMaker Autopilot training time and deployed inference endpoints separately from Redshift compute costs. Aurora PostgreSQL pgvector support is included with standard Aurora instance pricing.

databases.name: Databricks (MLflow + DBRX)
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI platform combining MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment lifecycle management with Mosaic AI for fine-tuning, serving, and evaluating LLMs including their own DBRX open-source foundation model. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database built into the Lakehouse that automatically syncs embeddings from Delta tables, supports real-time and batch embedding pipelines, and provides ANN search with metadata filtering. The platform integrates with Unity Catalog for governed access to models, embeddings, and training data across the entire ML lifecycle.
databases.llm_integration: Databricks supports serving DBRX, LLaMA, Mistral, and external models via Mosaic AI Model Serving with an OpenAI-compatible API. AI Functions in Databricks SQL allow calling LLMs directly from SQL queries using ai_query(), ai_summarize(), and ai_classify(). MLflow tracks experiments and manages model versions across the full training-to-production pipeline.
databases.pricing_notes: MLflow is open-source and free. Managed Databricks services including Vector Search, Model Serving, and AI Functions are billed via Databricks Units (DBUs) based on compute tier and usage duration. DBRX is open-source but serving it on Databricks incurs standard DBU costs for the inference compute.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing vector embeddings alongside operational document data in the same collection, querying them with the $vectorSearch aggregation pipeline stage using approximate nearest neighbor search powered by Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) indexing. This eliminates the need for a separate vector store by combining operational, analytical, and vector workloads in a single platform, supporting hybrid search that combines vector similarity with full-text search and metadata filters in a single query. Atlas integrates with major embedding providers and LLM frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Amazon Bedrock to support full RAG pipeline construction.
databases.llm_integration: Atlas Vector Search integrates natively with LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and Amazon Bedrock for embedding generation and LLM orchestration. MongoDB Atlas also offers Atlas Stream Processing and Data Federation for connecting AI pipelines to real-time and multi-source data.
databases.pricing_notes: Vector Search is available on Atlas M10 dedicated clusters and above. Pricing is based on the underlying Atlas cluster tier with no separate per-query charge for vector search itself. Storage costs apply to embedding data stored in collections. A free tier M0 cluster does not support Vector Search indexes.
